They say I'm done here Friday. I can't go back under the bridge with this leg. Where do I go?
Friday, and you can't go back under the bridge with that leg. That's a hard spot. I'll pass that along. Can you tell me how you get around now, like a walker, stairs, or a cane?
Walker, mostly. I can do a few steps if there's a rail, but stairs wear me out, so I need something on the ground floor or an elevator.
Walker, and stairs are hard, so ground floor or an elevator. Got it. Before Friday, what city were you living in before this, or where did you last sleep?
Santa Ana, mostly. I had a spot near the river for a while, then the bridge after that. I don't really want to get into the details of why I lost the room, though.
Santa Ana, near the river, then the bridge. Got it, and we won't go into why you lost the room. Have you served in the military at any point?
Nope, never served. Why do you ask?
Some programs open doors for veterans, so I ask everyone. Thanks for answering. Do you have a phone right now, and what kind is it?
Yeah, I've got a basic phone. It's just for calls and texts, no fancy internet stuff. Is that going to be a problem?
A basic phone for calls and texts is fine. I'm not saying whether it's a problem; the team will see it. Which language do you like to talk in?
English is fine.
English, got it. About how old are you? A range is fine, like 40s or over 60.
Sixty-two.

Here's what I heard: You leave Friday. You use a walker, and you need a ground floor or an elevator. You lived in Santa Ana, near the river and then under the bridge. You never served in the military. You have a basic phone for calls and texts. You speak English and you're 62. Did I get that right?

Yes, that's right. Friday, the walker, ground floor or elevator, Santa Ana, the river and then the bridge, never served, basic phone, English, and I'm 62. Also, I lost my ID, so I don't have anything to show anyone.
Thanks for telling me. Losing your ID is a big deal, and I'll note it. I'll pass all of this to your case manager, and we'll find your next step now.

transcript.text: Hola. Soy Sal. Estoy en esta tableta para ayudarte. No soy una persona, y alguien del equipo va a revisar todo contigo. Te voy a hacer unas preguntas cortas y tomar notas breves para tu administrador de caso. Puedes saltar cualquiera. ¿Qué es lo que más necesitas ahora?
Yo sé trabajar. Solo necesito como dos mil dólares para el equipo y el permiso.
Entiendo. Trabajas y necesitas unos dos mil dólares para tus herramientas y el permiso. ¿Qué tipo de trabajo haces?
Vendía comida en los tianguis, sobre todo tamales y aguas frescas. Tenía mi puesto los fines de semana y entre semana preparaba todo en la cocina de una amiga.
Tamales y aguas frescas, los fines de semana en el tianguis. Qué bien. ¿Tienes una cuenta de banco y alguna identificación, como una licencia o un ID?
No tengo cuenta de banco ahorita. Tengo un ID del estado, la de California, pero no sé si me van a pedir más papeles.
Tienes tu ID de California. Gracias por decirme. No te voy a decir qué papeles pedirán; eso lo verá tu equipo. ¿Dónde piensas dormir cuando salgas de aquí?
No sé todavía. Ahorita estoy quedándome en un lugar prestado, pero no es para siempre. Por eso necesito este trabajo.
Entiendo, un lugar prestado no es para siempre. Gracias por decírmelo. ¿En qué ciudad viviste por última vez antes de llegar aquí?
Aquí en Orange County, en Santa Ana. Viví en un cuarto que rentaba, hasta que ya no pude pagarlo.
Santa Ana, en un cuarto que rentabas. Gracias por contarme eso. ¿Tienes teléfono celular? Si es así, ¿es de botones o de pantalla, y puedes recibir mensajes?
Sí tengo celular, es de pantalla y tiene datos. Sí puedo recibir mensajes, pero a veces se me acaba la batería, así que mejor llámame o mándame mensaje en la mañana.
Un celular de pantalla con datos, y mejor en la mañana. Anotado. ¿Cuántos años tienes, más o menos? Un rango está bien, como en tus 30 o 40.
Tengo 41 años, en los cuarenta.

Esto es lo que escuché: sabes trabajar vendiendo tamales y aguas frescas en los tianguis, necesitas unos dos mil dólares para el equipo y el permiso, no tienes cuenta de banco, tienes tu ID de California, estás quedándote en un lugar prestado, viviste en Santa Ana, tienes un celular de pantalla con datos que es mejor usar en la mañana, y tienes 41 años. ¿Entendí bien?
Sí, eso es todo. Solo que lo de los tamales y las aguas frescas, lo hacía los fines de semana en el tianguis, y entre semana en la cocina de mi amiga.
Gracias por la aclaración. Entendido: los fines de semana en el tianguis y entre semana en la cocina de tu amiga. Ya tengo lo que necesito. Ahora voy a buscar tu siguiente paso.

transcript.text: Hi. I'm Sal, a helper on this tablet. I'm not a person, and a staff member will check everything with you. I'll ask a few short questions and take short notes for your case manager. You can skip any of them. What's on your mind most right now?
I don't hear well on the phone. Is there somebody I can go see?

I'm sorry, that makes it hard. I can't set up a visit myself, but I'll pass this along to your case manager so they can help you with it. Can I ask you one quick thing first: what language do you prefer?
English is fine, thank you. I can read things too, if that's easier than talking.

Thank you. English works, and I can keep things short and clear. Your case manager will know you'd rather read than talk on the phone. When you leave, what do you need most: a place to sleep, work, or getting home to family?
Honestly, I don't have anywhere to sleep tonight, and I don't have any income. I don't have family close by to go home to, so a place to stay is what I need most.
Thank you for telling me. So you need a place to sleep, and you have no income right now. Got it. Do you know how you'll get around when you leave, like with a walker, stairs, or a bunk?
I don't use a walker or anything like that. I get around fine, and I usually take the bus. Stairs are okay as long as there's a railing.
Good to know. You take the bus and do fine on stairs with a railing. Where did you live last, before the hospital?
I'd rather not get into that part right now. It's private, and I'm not ready to talk about it with you yet.
That's okay, we can skip it. Do you have a cell phone, or a phone at a place you can use?
I have an old cell phone, but it's hard for me to hear calls on it. Texting works much better for me, so please send me messages when you can.
Thanks, texting is much better for you, so I'll note that. Do you have ID, like a state ID or driver's license?
I have an old ID card from the DMV, I think it's still good. It's in my purse somewhere, and I can dig it out and bring it along when I come in.

Here's what I heard: you need a place to sleep and have no income right now. You get around fine, take the bus, and do okay on stairs with a railing. You'd rather text than talk on the phone. You have an old DMV ID card. Did I get that right?
Yes, that's right. You've got it all.
Thank you. I'll pass this to your case manager, and I'll find your next step now. Please bring that DMV ID when you come in.

entry.description: The DMV may issue an ID card at no fee to a person who is homeless as defined by the McKinney-Vento Act, and at a reduced fee to people who meet income requirements for certain assistance programs. Applications are finished in person at a DMV office.

entry.name: Free certified birth certificate for people experiencing homelessness (AB 1733 / AB 2490)
entry.hours: 8:00 a.m. - 4:30 p.m. Monday - Friday
entry.notes: Medium confidence: the State page and affidavit establish the right, but the Orange County Clerk-Recorder pages fetched (vital records page and fee schedule effective 2026-09-01) do not mention the fee exemption or how to present the affidavit, so call first. Phone, address and hours are the Clerk-Recorder's Central Office, for people born in Orange County; branches are at 222 S. Harbor Blvd, Ste. 110A, Anaheim and 24031 El Toro Rd., Ste. 150, Laguna Hills (9:00 a.m. - 4:30 p.m.). People born elsewhere apply to that county or the State. The affidavit lists who counts as a homeless services provider, including a nonprofit agency funded to serve homeless people. In-person applicants must fill in the application online first and bring valid government photo ID, which can be circular for someone with no ID.
entry.description: California law lets a person who is homeless get a certified copy of their birth record without a fee, from the county where they were born or from the State Registrar, using an Affidavit of Homeless Status signed by a homeless services provider.
entry.cost: No fee with a completed affidavit; the Orange County Clerk-Recorder fee schedule otherwise lists a birth certificate at $34.00
